questions.q: What does `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW vw_unpaid_invoices_over_threshold AS SELECT ...` do?
options: Runs the query once and discards the result
Deletes the underlying tables
Saves the query under a name, as a reusable, table-like object that can be queried repeatedly
Permanently changes the data in ap_invoices_all
questions.explain: A view stores a named, reusable query definition that behaves like a table whenever it's queried, without duplicating data.

questions.q: What does `OR REPLACE` accomplish in `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`?
options: It allows re-running the statement to update the view's definition instead of raising an error if the view already exists
It deletes all data from the view
It is required syntax with no functional effect
It converts the view into a physical table
questions.explain: OR REPLACE lets you redefine an existing view safely, rather than having to drop it first or hit an error.

questions.q: Once `vw_unpaid_invoices_over_threshold` is created, what does a user need to know to query it?
options: The full three-table join and all three filter conditions underneath it
They must re-create the view every time they query it
They need direct access to AP_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL specifically
Nothing beyond how to SELECT from it like any other table — the underlying complexity is hidden inside the view's definition
questions.explain: A view hides its underlying query complexity — users can SELECT from it as if it were a simple table.

questions.q: What is the limitation this lesson highlights about hardcoding `10000` and `30` directly into a view's definition?
options: There is no limitation — views automatically adjust to any threshold
If the thresholds need to change often, the view itself must be edited and re-created each time, since it isn't automatically parameterized
Views cannot contain any numeric literals
Hardcoded values make the view run slower than a script
questions.explain: A view's definition is fixed until explicitly altered; frequently-changing thresholds may be better served by a documented script or a parameterized BI report.
